lines.text: The army broke camp three days after the duel. The war was won, the river was ours, and every lord in House Varr wanted to shake my hand.
The same lords who had laughed at my farmers. Now they wanted to buy my turnips, borrow my blacksmith, and marry their daughters to the zero.
That one keeps staring at you. The lord with the moustache.
He wants to sell me his daughter.
Should I shoot him?
You have a problem, Wren.
On the last night, my father sent for me again. This time there was no map on the table. Just two cups of wine.
You did well.
Three words. I had waited sixteen years for them. I didn't know what to do with my hands.
Now listen to me carefully. Go home. Tomorrow, at first light. Take your people and go back to Greyhollow, and stay there.
Father, the lords want trade agreements. If I stay, I could...
Go home, Lucan.
He had never said my name like that before. Not like an order. Like a man who was afraid.
And if anyone, anyone, asks you to touch a Measuring Stone again, you refuse. Do you understand me?
Why?
He looked at me for a long time. Then he drank his wine, and said nothing at all.
We left at first light. Nine days later, Greyhollow's gate came into view. And standing in front of it, arms folded, exactly where I'd left him, was Bram.
You're late, my lord.
We won a war.
Did you bring them all back?
Every one.
Bram nodded once. Then he turned away very quickly, and said there was something in his eye. There wasn't.
Far to the south, in a house that had lost its war, Lady Sabine Corrow wrote a letter. Not to her husband. Not to the king.
To the Grand Measurer of the Order. Regarding a boy who reads as zero, in a village where nobody stays common.
And in the capital, beneath the Cathedral of the Seven, a man in white robes read that letter by candlelight.
A hollow-born. After all these years.
Send the Measurers north.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fourteen, coming soon.
